newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK FINMIN SEES $250 MLN, 5-YR EUROBOND END OCT.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK FINMIN SEES $250 MLN, 5-YR EUROBOND END OCT.

text.p: Slovakia will launch a $250 million tranche of five-year, Eurobonds by the end of October in an issue lead-managed by Nomura International Plc, the Finance Ministry said on Wednesday.

"This $250 million will be the minimum offer, the final sum will depend o the interest in the bond, and it may be increased to some $300 million," Jaroslav Nahlik, head of ministry's international financial institutions department, told Reuters.
Nahlik said Slovakia will also draw a $70 million bridge loan from Nomura by the end of July to be repaid from funds from the bond issue later this year.
"This short-term credit will be repaid from what Nomura obtains after the issue of our Eurobonds," Nahlik said.
He would not give any information on the Eurobond's rate, nor on the pricing of the bridging loan.
The $70 million credit will be used to boost the basic capital of a newly-created Export-Import bank expected to begin operations this summer.
The remainder of the Eurobond issue will help cover motorway construction for this year, originally planned to be financed by the state budget.

The finance ministry said last week that the original idea how to obtain funds for the ExIm bank and motorway construction was to draw a loan with the hope of negotiating better terms, but the governemnt later changed the plan to the Eurobond issue.
The Slovak Republic carries a sovereign debt rating from Standard & Poor's of BBB-, and Baa3 from Moody's.
